name: OpenSea
rootCause: According to OpenSea's official tweet, hackers sent phishing emails to all users' mailboxes at the same time as the OpenSea contract was upgraded. Many users mistakenly thought it was an official email and authorized the wallet, which resulted in the wallet being stolen. OpenSea co-founder and CEO Devin Finzer confirmed the phishing attack in a tweet.

descriptions.text: According to OpenSea's official tweet, hackers sent phishing emails to all users' mailboxes at the same time as the OpenSea contract was upgraded. Many users mistakenly thought it was an official email and authorized the wallet, which resulted in the wallet being stolen. OpenSea co-founder and CEO Devin Finzer confirmed the phishing attack in a tweet.

On 20 February 2022, OpenSea users were targeted by a phishing campaign that tricked them into signing approvals for a malicious contract, enabling the attacker to transfer valuable NFTs without needing the victims' seed phrases or passwords. Around 28 wallets lost NFTs worth approximately $2 million. The attacker sent forged emails mimicking OpenSea communications, prompting victims to interact with a phishing site. This site induced users to sign permissions granting a malicious contract the ability to transfer NFTs using the Wyvern protocol's exchange functionality. The exploit relied on victims trusting the email and unwittingly signing transactions enabling unauthorized transfers.
